001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.lang.System.Logger.Level;
004import java.util.ArrayList;
005import java.util.List;
006import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
007import java.util.concurrent.atomic.LongAdder;
008
009import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.CaseChanging;
010
011/**
012 * Numeric metrics about the logging system itself. Counters track running totals such as
013 * dropped events; gauges track values that can rise and fall, such as queued events.
014 * Unlike {@link LogAlerts}, updating a metric does not create an alert or notify
015 * listeners. Retain a {@link Gauge} for frequent updates without a name lookup.
016 * <p>
017 * An instance is available from every {@link LogConfig#metrics()}. Components that are
018 * {@linkplain LogProvider provided} config, or that are
019 * {@linkplain LogLifecycle#start( LogConfig) started} with config, should prefer
020 * capturing {@code config.metrics()} over reaching for global state.
021 * <p>
022 * Deliberately a separate type from {@link LogAlerts} rather than more methods on it -
023 * the two are meant to be independently replaceable (e.g. a future Micrometer-backed
024 * {@code LogMetrics} without needing to also replace how alerts are recorded).
025 *
026 * @see LogConfig#metrics()
027 */
028public sealed interface LogMetrics permits DefaultLogMetrics {
029
030        /**
031         * Counter name for the global count of log events dropped without ever being written
032         * anywhere - for example an appender dropping events on reentry. Incremented whenever
033         * a drop happens regardless of whether that particular drop is also logged/alerted,
034         * since counting and alerting/logging are separate concerns.
035         */
036        static final String EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC = "events.dropped";
037
038        /**
039         * Gauge name for the aggregate number of events waiting in async publisher buffers.
040         * Events removed for processing are no longer counted, even while their output is
041         * being written. Concurrent snapshots can briefly lead or lag queue activity.
042         */
043        static final String EVENTS_QUEUED_METRIC = "events.queued";
044
045        /**
046         * Counter name for the global count of times a reused encoder buffer had its backing
047         * storage shrunk back down after growing past its configured max size (see
048         * {@link LogEncoder.Buffer#isOversized()}). An occasional trim is normal and expected
049         * once in a while, but resizing <em>often</em> is a sign the configured max size (or
050         * the initial size) doesn't match the actual event sizes being logged - worth
051         * watching, not erroring on, hence {@link #warnCounter(String, long)} rather than
052         * {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}.
053         */
054        static final String BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC = "buffer.trimmed";
055
056        /**
057         * Counter name for the global count of log events an appender failed to write - the
058         * encoder or output threw while appending, so the event was caught, alerted (see
059         * {@link LogAlerts#error(Class, String, Throwable)}), and lost rather than retried.
060         * Kept separate from {@link #EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC}: a drop is a deliberate skip (the
061         * appender chose not to write), while this is an unexpected failure partway through
062         * actually trying to - different root causes worth distinguishing when triaging.
063         */
064        static final String EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC = "events.failed";
065
066        /**
067         * Counter name for the global count of failed appender output reopen attempts. Each
068         * failed attempt increments this counter in addition to recording an alert,
069         * regardless of the appender or output type.
070         */
071        static final String REOPEN_FAIL_METRIC = "reopen.fail";
072
073        /**
074         * Counter name for the global count of appender output reopen attempts, whether
075         * successful or failed. Subtract {@link #REOPEN_FAIL_METRIC} to obtain the number of
076         * successful attempts.
077         */
078        static final String REOPEN_METRIC = "reopen";
079
080        /**
081         * Counter name for failed automatic file rotation attempts, including closing the
082         * active output, rotating archives, and opening the replacement output. Recovery
083         * attempts that fail also increment this counter. External rotation followed by an
084         * explicit reopen is counted by {@link #REOPEN_FAIL_METRIC} instead. Events lost
085         * because rotation failed are also counted by {@link #EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC}.
086         */
087        static final String ROLL_FAIL_METRIC = "roll.fail";
088
089        /**
090         * Counter name for the running count of distinct logger names registered via
091         * {@link LogConfig.LoggerRegistry#registerLoggerName(LoggerAPI, String)}. Not itself
092         * a problem, hence {@link #infoCounter(String, long)} rather than
093         * {@link #warnCounter(String, long)}, but worth watching: a count that keeps climbing
094         * without bound is a sign something is using per-request/per-entity data (e.g. a
095         * request id) as a logger name instead of a fixed, bounded set of names.
096         */
097        static final String LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC = "logger.names";
098
099        /**
100         * Increments a counter for something worth tracking as "this happens and it matters".
101         * @param name counter name, e.g. {@link #EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC} or a logger name.
102         * @param increment amount to add, usually {@code 1}.
103         */
104        public void errorCounter(String name, long increment);
105
106        /**
107         * Like {@link #errorCounter(String, long)} but for something worth tracking yet less
108         * significant than an error - a trend worth watching rather than something that, by
109         * itself, indicates a problem. Kept as a separate counter namespace from
110         * {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}: the same {@code name} passed to both is two
111         * distinct counters, not one shared one.
112         * @param name counter name, e.g. {@link #BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC}.
113         * @param increment amount to add, usually {@code 1}.
114         */
115        public void warnCounter(String name, long increment);
116
117        /**
118         * Like {@link #errorCounter(String, long)} but for a plain running total, not
119         * inherently a problem or even a trend worth watching. Kept as a separate counter
120         * namespace from
121         * {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}/{@link #warnCounter(String, long)}: the same
122         * {@code name} passed to more than one of these is a distinct counter per method, not
123         * one shared one.
124         * @param name counter name, e.g. {@link #LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC}.
125         * @param increment amount to add, usually {@code 1}.
126         */
127        public void infoCounter(String name, long increment);
128
129        /**
130         * Creates a handle for updating a named value directly. For INFO, WARNING, and ERROR,
131         * each call returns a new handle sharing the value for the same name and level;
132         * retain the handle for frequent updates without repeated name lookups. The value is
133         * initially zero and appears in {@link #snapshot()} as soon as the handle is created.
134         * Counter methods for the same name and level share this value too. Levels below INFO
135         * and OFF return a shared no-op handle and do not register a metric.
136         * @param name metric name.
137         * @param level significance of the metric.
138         * @return a handle to the shared value, or a no-op handle.
139         */
140        public Gauge gauge(String name, Level level);
141
142        /**
143         * A retained handle for incrementing or decrementing a metric. Updates are thread
144         * safe and do not perform a name lookup. Read the value through {@link #snapshot()}.
145         */
146        sealed interface Gauge permits DefaultGauge, NoopGauge {
147
148                /**
149                 * Returns a shared gauge that ignores all updates. Use it until a metric is
150                 * available, or when metric collection is disabled.
151                 * @return no-op gauge.
152                 */
153                public static Gauge noop() {
154                        return NoopGauge.NOOP;
155                }
156
157                /**
158                 * Increments the value by one.
159                 */
160                public void increment();
161
162                /**
163                 * Adds the supplied amount.
164                 * @param increment amount to add.
165                 */
166                public void increment(long increment);
167
168                /**
169                 * Decrements the value by one.
170                 */
171                public void decrement();
172
173                /**
174                 * Subtracts the supplied amount.
175                 * @param decrement amount to subtract.
176                 */
177                public void decrement(long decrement);
178
179        }
180
181        /**
182         * A snapshot of every metric recorded via {@link #errorCounter(String, long)},
183         * {@link #warnCounter(String, long)}, {@link #infoCounter(String, long)}, and
184         * {@link #gauge(String, Level)}. Counter values increase over time; gauge values can
185         * also decrease. Snapshots are approximate while updates are concurrent.
186         * @return immutable snapshot.
187         */
188        public List<Metric> snapshot();
189
190        /**
191         * A single named metric's current value, as returned by {@link #snapshot()}.
192         *
193         * @param name metric name, as passed to a counter method or
194         * {@link #gauge(String, Level)}.
195         * @param level significance of the metric. Counter methods use {@link Level#ERROR},
196         * {@link Level#WARNING}, or {@link Level#INFO}; gauges use the level supplied to
197         * {@link #gauge(String, Level)}.
198         * @param value current value, which can decrease for a gauge.
199         */
200        record Metric(String name, Level level, long value) {
201        }
202
203        /**
204         * The fixed, well known set of metrics RainbowGum itself records, as opposed to the
205         * open ended, per logger name counters {@link LogAlerts#alert(LogEvent)} also drives
206         * into the counter matching the alert's level. Enumerable on purpose: consumers that
207         * want to bind every well known counter to something else (a Micrometer counter or
208         * gauge per constant, for example) can loop over {@link #values()} instead of hand
209         * listing each {@code String}/{@link Level} pair themselves.
210         */
211        @CaseChanging
212        enum StandardMetric {
213
214                /**
215                 * See {@link #EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC}.
216                 */
217                EVENTS_DROPPED(EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC, Level.ERROR),
218                /**
219                 * See {@link #EVENTS_QUEUED_METRIC}.
220                 */
221                EVENTS_QUEUED(EVENTS_QUEUED_METRIC, Level.INFO, true),
222                /**
223                 * See {@link #BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC}.
224                 */
225                BUFFER_TRIMMED(BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC, Level.WARNING),
226                /**
227                 * See {@link #EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC}.
228                 */
229                EVENTS_FAILED(EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC, Level.ERROR),
230                /**
231                 * See {@link #LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC}.
232                 */
233                LOGGER_NAMES(LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC, Level.INFO),
234                /**
235                 * See {@link #REOPEN_FAIL_METRIC}.
236                 */
237                REOPEN_FAIL(REOPEN_FAIL_METRIC, Level.ERROR),
238                /**
239                 * See {@link #REOPEN_METRIC}.
240                 */
241                REOPEN(REOPEN_METRIC, Level.INFO),
242                /**
243                 * See {@link #ROLL_FAIL_METRIC}.
244                 */
245                ROLL_FAIL(ROLL_FAIL_METRIC, Level.ERROR);
246
247                private final String metricName;
248
249                private final Level level;
250
251                private final boolean gauge;
252
253                StandardMetric(String metricName, Level level) {
254                        this(metricName, level, false);
255                }
256
257                StandardMetric(String metricName, Level level, boolean gauge) {
258                        this.metricName = metricName;
259                        this.level = level;
260                        this.gauge = gauge;
261                }
262
263                /**
264                 * The metric name, as passed to a counter method or {@link #gauge(String, Level)}
265                 * and matched against {@link Metric#name()}.
266                 * @return metric name.
267                 */
268                public String metricName() {
269                        return metricName;
270                }
271
272                /**
273                 * The significance of this metric, also exposed through {@link Metric#level()} in
274                 * {@link #snapshot()}.
275                 * @return level.
276                 */
277                public Level level() {
278                        return level;
279                }
280
281                /**
282                 * Whether this metric can decrease and should be bound as a gauge instead of an
283                 * increasing counter.
284                 * @return true for a gauge.
285                 */
286                public boolean isGauge() {
287                        return gauge;
288                }
289
290        }
291
292}
293
294final class DefaultLogMetrics implements LogMetrics {
295
296        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, LongAdder> errorCounters = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
297
298        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, LongAdder> warnCounters = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
299
300        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, LongAdder> infoCounters = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
301
302        @Override
303        public Gauge gauge(String name, Level level) {
304                return switch (level) {
305                        case ERROR -> new DefaultGauge(errorCounters.computeIfAbsent(name, k -> new LongAdder()));
306                        case WARNING -> new DefaultGauge(warnCounters.computeIfAbsent(name, k -> new LongAdder()));
307                        case INFO -> new DefaultGauge(infoCounters.computeIfAbsent(name, k -> new LongAdder()));
308                        case ALL, TRACE, DEBUG, OFF -> NoopGauge.NOOP;
309                };
310        }
311
312        @Override
313        public void errorCounter(String name, long increment) {
314                errorCounters.computeIfAbsent(name, k -> new LongAdder()).add(increment);
315        }
316
317        @Override
318        public void warnCounter(String name, long increment) {
319                warnCounters.computeIfAbsent(name, k -> new LongAdder()).add(increment);
320        }
321
322        @Override
323        public void infoCounter(String name, long increment) {
324                infoCounters.computeIfAbsent(name, k -> new LongAdder()).add(increment);
325        }
326
327        @Override
328        public List<Metric> snapshot() {
329                List<Metric> list = new ArrayList<>(errorCounters.size() + warnCounters.size() + infoCounters.size());
330                for (var e : errorCounters.entrySet()) {
331                        list.add(new Metric(e.getKey(), Level.ERROR, e.getValue().sum()));
332                }
333                for (var e : warnCounters.entrySet()) {
334                        list.add(new Metric(e.getKey(), Level.WARNING, e.getValue().sum()));
335                }
336                for (var e : infoCounters.entrySet()) {
337                        list.add(new Metric(e.getKey(), Level.INFO, e.getValue().sum()));
338                }
339                return List.copyOf(list);
340        }
341
342}
343
344final class DefaultGauge implements LogMetrics.Gauge {
345
346        private final LongAdder value;
347
348        DefaultGauge(LongAdder value) {
349                this.value = value;
350        }
351
352        @Override
353        public void increment() {
354                value.increment();
355        }
356
357        @Override
358        public void increment(long increment) {
359                value.add(increment);
360        }
361
362        @Override
363        public void decrement() {
364                value.decrement();
365        }
366
367        @Override
368        public void decrement(long decrement) {
369                value.add(-decrement);
370        }
371
372}
373
374enum NoopGauge implements LogMetrics.Gauge {
375
376        NOOP;
377
378        @Override
379        public void increment() {
380        }
381
382        @Override
383        public void increment(long increment) {
384        }
385
386        @Override
387        public void decrement() {
388        }
389
390        @Override
391        public void decrement(long decrement) {
392        }
393
394}
